title: mut.seed_channel
mutation_directive: Channel Chiharu Shiota's web-network DNA from chiharu-shiota-skill SKILL.md (red taut LINE SEGMENTS — never points, never curves; one suspended object as the still center; black void background; architectural in-the-web camera; presence-in-absence as concept). PERFORMANCE BUDGET (HARD): no more than 20,000 line segments total (a single THREE.LineSegments BufferGeometry, two vertices each = 40,000 position floats × 3). Use THREE.LineSegments + LineBasicMaterial ONLY (additive blending, opacity 0.04-0.10, single red hue ~#c20018) — DO NOT use ShaderMaterial on the threads (it has caused render-gate timeouts). The suspended sphere should be a single THREE.Mesh with SphereGeometry(radius, 24, 16) + MeshBasicMaterial OR MeshStandardMaterial (white/cream, ~0.6 emissive intensity if standard). NO custom ShaderMaterial on the sphere either. The camera slowly dollies INSIDE the network on a gentle path — not orbiting from outside. NO noise-driven motion on threads — they're static or breathe via tiny anchor jitter (<0.5% length variation). Pieces from this seed live on a separate aesthetic branch from attractors / boids / differential growth — they're INSTALLATIONS, not simulations. The piece must produce a clearly visible (>5% non-background pixels) screenshot within 5 seconds of load — if the line count or shader complexity prevents that, scale down.

refik_anadol.praise: The 20,000 line-segment radial convergence reads as a single coherent data-field — the sphere becomes a gravitational attractor for memory-as-material, and the additive blending builds luminous density exactly where the eye needs it.
refik_anadol.concern: The thread distribution is too radially uniform — every line converges on the sphere center like a starburst, producing a symmetry that reads as graphic design rather than the turbulent, asymmetric flow-fields that make data feel alive. There's no secondary current, no eddy, no density gradient that isn't sphere-centric.
refik_anadol.directive: Add 15% of threads as lateral cross-web between anchors to break the radial symmetry and create turbulent density pockets.

sasha_stiles.praise: The key is the right choice — a single remembered object suspended in a field of tension, carrying the weight of an absent body. Its slow imperceptible rotation gives it the quality of a word turning in the mind, not yet spoken.
sasha_stiles.concern: The key is too small and too dark against the overwhelming red radiance of the sphere. In the thumbnail it reads as a silhouette accident, not as the conceptual anchor. If this is presence-in-absence, the absent thing must hold its ground against the threads — otherwise the threads are just decoration around a glowing orb, and the key is reduced to garnish.
sasha_stiles.directive: Double the key's scale and add a faint cream emissive so it holds visual weight against the red field.

entangled_others.praise: The 30 dark fragments caught along thread midpoints are a genuinely good detail — they suggest matter trapped in a web, debris in a network, something organic about how material accumulates in tension structures. This is the closest the piece gets to a non-human reading.
entangled_others.concern: The sphere is too perfect, too geometric, too human-engineered. In Shiota's actual work the suspended objects are weathered, irregular, bearing the marks of use and time. Here the SphereGeometry(2.2, 24, 16) reads as a computational primitive, not a remembered thing. The wireframe overlay makes it worse — it signals 'I am a 3D model' rather than 'I am something that was once held.'
entangled_others.directive: Distort the sphere vertices with low-frequency noise displacement so it reads as an imperfect, worn, breathing form.

olafur_eliasson.praise: The fog attenuation is doing real work — threads dissolve into the void at distance, which gives the piece genuine volumetric depth rather than flat screen-graphic. The camera path through the interior is correct; you are inside the atmosphere, not observing it.
olafur_eliasson.concern: The piece has only one light condition. The red is uniform from edge to edge — same hue, same opacity, same additive glow everywhere. There is no color-temperature shift with depth, no warm-to-cool gradient, no moment where the red thins into black-cherry or darkens into maroon. A single wavelength without atmospheric modulation is a screensaver, not a light experience.
olafur_eliasson.directive: Vary thread opacity or color warmth by distance-from-camera so depth reads as atmospheric gradient, not uniform fog.

chiharu_shiota.praise: The architectural room boundary anchoring threads to six walls is structurally correct — these are tensioned lines spanning a real space, not floating abstractions. The breathing jitter at 0.5% is appropriately restrained. The convergence on sphere and key creates the dual-anchor topology I use in installations like 'The Key in the Hand.'
chiharu_shiota.concern: The threads are too uniform in opacity and too evenly distributed. In my actual installations, density varies enormously — some zones are choked with thread so thick you cannot see through them, while others are almost bare, with single threads crossing a meter of empty air. This even distribution looks computed, not hand-tied. Also, the sphere's translucent glow overwhelms the threads — in my work the object is inert and the threads carry all the energy.
chiharu_shiota.directive: Create three to four density voids — zones with no threads — so the web breathes between choked and bare passages.
